label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Tolu, I’m literally the person you’re looking for 😭 I’m in Biology 100L now. JAMB 2025 I scored 251, applied for Medicine and Surgery and got Biology in a federal uni here in Lagos.

First, I’m sorry. I know people are already throwing “accept it” and “rewrite” at you, but when you’ve had your mind on Medicine and you open your portal to see something else, it hurts. The day I saw Biology, I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t even eat. So please don’t feel silly for crying.

My mum was still telling people in church I was doing Medicine for like two months after 😭 I actually had to beg her to stop because it was making everything harder. Family expectations can add their own pressure to an already confusing situation.

**About the transfer:** it’s real in my school, so I don’t think Kingsley is right to call it a myth everywhere. But favour saying “just read hard” also makes it sound much simpler than it is.

What our level adviser told us is that to be considered for transfer to MBBS after 100L, we need a CGPA of at least **4.5 out of 5**, AND there has to be space. She also said we need to have met the Medicine cut-offs in both JAMB and post-UTME. According to her, about six people were moved in from the whole faculty last year, and she thinks over 40 applied. So yes, people can get in, but it’s competitive and meeting the CGPA alone doesn’t guarantee it.

Please don’t use my school’s rules to make your decision for yours. I don’t know your school’s Medicine cut-offs or your post-UTME score, so your 268 alone doesn’t tell us whether you qualify for transfer. **Go to your faculty or department and ask them for the exact rules for your school**: the required CGPA, JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs, whether they actually accept transfers into Medicine, and how availability of space works. If you can, ask how many people have transferred recently too. Don’t just trust forum people, including me 😅 And since your acceptance fee deadline is in two weeks, I’d try to ask them as soon as possible.

On my own end, my CGPA after first semester is 4.31. It’s not 4.5, but I’m still trying. I’m telling you that so you know I’m not speaking as somebody who has already transferred or pretending the target is easy.

As for what Biology 100L is like, we do BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people in my set 😂 You still have to put in work across the courses, especially if you’re aiming for that kind of CGPA. There are also practical expenses to think about: my lab coat was ₦6,500, dissecting kit ₦9,000, and the practical manual was extra.

But Biology itself is not a bad course. I’m enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected. In our first BIO practical, we dissected toads and one guy in my group fainted 😭 I was fine, and somehow that was the day I realised I actually like this thing. I still wanted Medicine, but I started seeing that Biology wasn’t just some punishment I had been given.

That doesn’t mean you have to suddenly love it or give up on Medicine. It just means your question is a fair one: maybe some of the pain is because you had your heart set on something else, rather than because Biology is a bad course. Give yourself room to find out how you actually feel about it.

On rewriting, I won’t tell you it’s wrong. If Medicine is what you really want and you’re ready for another JAMB and post-UTME attempt, that’s a valid choice. But staying home and trying again isn’t always as simple as “one year is nothing” either. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and is still at home. That doesn’t mean the same thing will happen to you, but it’s worth thinking about the possibility, not just the best-case outcome.

I’d also ask yourself one uncomfortable question: **do you want Medicine for yourself, or is it mainly that you want to be “doctor” for your parents?** It can be hard to separate the two when everybody has had expectations for you. There’s no need to answer anybody on this forum, just be honest with yourself.

If you accept Biology, please accept it knowing transfer is possible *if your school allows it*, but it is not automatic and may not happen. Ask yourself whether you could see yourself continuing in Biology if it doesn’t. And if you rewrite, go into it knowing it can take longer than you hoped, even when you work hard.

I know none of that makes the decision magically easy. Just try to get the actual information from your school before the deadline, then choose based on what you can live with—not what strangers are shouting at you to do. Whatever you decide, this is not the end of the world. You’ll be okay, Tolu ❤️
